title: devbin has no Homebrew formula and installs only from a local checkout -- brew install it on macOS and Linux, from its release tag, as the machine install projects vendor from
body:
FOUND 2026-10-14: hv, to vc in session, "devbin doesn't have a brew piepline at all, so we need to make one now", beside "I want BOTH devbin and intent work from 'brew install' and for them to BOTH work seamlessly on Unix (the kovacs VM in this case)". Restated the same morning through another estate's session: through Homebrew on macOS and Linux, with nothing installed from a local repository. Intent's formula is Intent's work (intent/vc); this issue is devbin's half.

WHAT EXISTS, read by vc at main 1a53cae7, whose lib/ is 99dd3106's:
- No formula and no tap: `brew info devbin` finds nothing.
- A machine install is published from devbin's own checkout with `bin/devbin install --prefix <dir>` (help install, "What a machine install is"), by default to install.prefix (~/Devel/opt/devbin in devbin's own config.yaml), and recorded in $XDG_DATA_HOME/devbin/home. Projects vendor from it with `install --into` and `upgrade --from`, and find it again through that line or DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX. An install answers only install, shell-init and version.
- bin/devbin follows symlinks to its real location, relative ones included, before it looks for its runtime (bin/devbin:35-42), so a link in Homebrew's bin/ into the keg finds the keg's runtime.
- devbin's own release config declares no after: (bin/.devbin/config.yaml:38-46).
- devbin's repository is private (gh repo view, 2026-10-14). Decision 32 has it going public in October or November.

THE MODEL is Utilz's formula (matthewsinclair/homebrew-utilz): it fetches the release tag and its commit by git, runs the tool's own installer into the keg (`bin/utilz install --prefix libexec --managed-by brew`) and links the dispatcher into bin/. devbin's PUBLISH is that installer already. Homebrew stages a git-fetched source with its .git (download_strategy/git_download_strategy.rb), which PUBLISH's clean-tree and provenance checks need, as Utilz's install does.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO (cc builds it and vc reviews it):
- A formula, kept in devbin's tree outside the published set, as Utilz keeps its own. It fetches the release tag and its commit by git, runs `bin/devbin install --prefix libexec`, and links bin/devbin into bin/. It depends on bash on macOS, whose /bin/bash 3.2 devbin refuses (directive 7); what a single verb needs is reported by `doctor`, never installed by the formula. Its test runs `devbin --version` and matches the tag.
- A tap, matthewsinclair/homebrew-devbin, named as Intent's and Utilz's are. Creating it is publishing, and its visibility is hv's call.
- A release step: the cut writes the new tag and its commit into the formula from git, never typed (Utilz's tools/formula-bump), and the tap receives it, through an after: in devbin's release config.
- Projects find the brew install with nothing installed from a local repository. Homebrew's sandbox cannot write the home line at install time (Intent's formula records that measurement), so the lookup gains a default: with no DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX and no home line, the brew install at Homebrew's opt/devbin path, which survives `brew upgrade` where the versioned Cellar keg does not (Intent's 0527). A home line that names something else still wins, so a machine set up from a checkout is not moved, and `doctor` says which install a project resolves to and what chose it. On hv's machines the home line is moved to the brew install at rollout.
- While the repository is private, `brew install` fetches with the user's own GitHub credentials. Measure which url form works under Homebrew on this Mac and on kovacs, where gh is signed in over ssh. Once devbin is public, the same formula works for anyone.
- Proof on this Mac and on kovacs (Ubuntu 26.04.1 on aarch64, uutils coreutils, Homebrew on Linux): `brew install` from the tap; `devbin --version`; `devbin install --into` seeds a fixture project; `bin/devbin upgrade` in that project finds the brew install; and after a `brew upgrade` to a later tag it still does. Before a tag carries the formula, rehearse from a local formula against a local clone, and say which half was rehearsed and which was not.
- Pages: help install, where it says what a machine install is and how a project finds one, and the README's install section.

NOT THIS ISSUE'S: Intent's Linux binaries and formula (intent/vc, ST0081), and ST0008's D55, since devbin's formula fetches by git and needs no CI-built asset. It ships in the next release, with everything open.

## Resolution

Landed at 93259543 on a green full suite (vc's, 2329 of 2329 ok, 0 not ok, 5 skipped, .errors empty, seal 20261016-0917; a first run, 20261016-0858, failed only fullcycle.bats:1020 (0096), a wall-clock bound under load that this change does not touch, filed on its own).

- **A formula, kept in devbin's tree outside the published set.** `packaging/homebrew/devbin.rb` fetches the release tag and its commit by git, depends on bash on macOS, runs `bin/devbin install --prefix libexec --managed-by brew`, links bin/devbin into bin/, and tests `devbin --version` against the version. It is a template with one tag placeholder and one revision placeholder.
- **The release step fills it from git.** `bin/devbin formula render <tag> <out>` reads the commit with `git rev-parse <tag>^{commit}` and refuses a tag or a template it cannot fill, writing nothing. `bin/devbin formula publish [--tap <url>]` renders the newest release, by the rule the release core's --patch reads, into a fresh clone of the tap, commits it and pushes it; a tap already carrying it publishes nothing, and a template with uncommitted changes is refused. **No `after:` is declared and the tap does not exist:** creating the tap is publishing, and whether it exists and how visible it is are hv's to decide. docs/releasing.md says how to add the `after:` line once it does.
- **The url while the repository is private** is `ssh://git@github.com/matthewsinclair/devbin.git`. Measured under Homebrew 7 on this Mac: the scp-like form is refused as not a URI, and https fails inside the fetch sandbox, which denies ~/Library/Keychains, with HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN set or not; the ssh URI fetches through the agent. At publication it becomes https, one line.
- **Projects find the brew install with nothing installed from a local repository.** With no DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX and no machine pointer, the machine install is `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/devbin/libexec`, which survives `brew upgrade`; a pointer or DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX still wins. doctor names the install a project resolves to and what chose it. A publish records the whole history of its checkout as ancestry, so a fresh keg places a project's commit as behind or level. shell-init and every hint name a keg by its opt link.
- **devbin steps aside from the keg.** An install published `--managed-by brew` is refused by devbin's own install and upgrade, which name `brew upgrade devbin`. A manifest that cannot be read is refused by each writer's own refusal (0144), and a keg is left unchanged under it.
- **Pages:** help install, upgrade, shell-init, doctor and formula, the README's Homebrew section (which names the tap as not yet created), and docs/releasing.md.
- **Proof.** Rehearsed on this Mac on 2026-10-16 from a local tap against a local clone with local tags, the url rewritten to that clone: brew install, brew test, `devbin --version`, audit, `devbin install --into` a fixture, a bare `bin/devbin upgrade` finding the brew install, and after `brew upgrade` to a later tag, doctor reading moved on and upgrade finding it again. **The network half, the ssh fetch from GitHub, was not rehearsed**, and neither was kovacs: both wait on the tap. Homebrew's formulae, versions, pins, taps and trust file were left as they were found, but for an earlier rehearsal tap, untapped as intended, and except that four build dependencies brew autoremoved during the rehearsal were reinstalled at the same versions with their receipts' installed_as_dependency now null, the old value lost; a brew run under a scratch XDG_CONFIG_HOME now sets HOMEBREW_NO_AUTOREMOVE=1.

Declared:
- rollout on hv's machines: delete the machine pointer or write the opt path into it verbatim, never through install_pointer_write or physical_dir, which resolve it to the Cellar keg;
- ancestry comes from the checkout's history, so a history rewrite at publication makes every older vendored commit read unknown, and the fleet then needs a forced re-vendor or an old-to-new map;
- the proof on kovacs, Linux's sandbox, uutils and the real url, is not done.
